Title: HealMe: Harnessing Cognitive Reframing in Large Language Models for Psychotherapy
Venue: Proceedings of the 62nd Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics (Volume 1: Long Papers)
Raw Eval Metrics: Empathy (0-3 points), Logical Coherence (0-3 points), Guidance (0-3 points), Overall Score (0-3 points); Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS)
Agreement Method: Average Difference (Avg. Diff) and Standard Deviation (Std. Dev)

Title: AnnaAgent: Dynamic Evolution Agent System with Multi-Session Memory for Realistic Seeker Simulation
Venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: ACL 2025
Temporal_Modeling_Details: Within a single session, emotions are dynamically inferred per utterance and perturbed, and chief complaints evolve in stages via a chain with stage-switching logic. Across sessions, a tertiary memory mechanism divides memory into real-time (current conversation), short-term (recent events and self-report scale changes), and long-term (previous sessions' conversations and scales scheduled via Agentic RAG), with a querier retrieving previous session content when relevant.
Raw Eval Metrics: BERT-score (Anthropomorphism), G-Eval (Personality Fidelity), G-Eval (Long-term Memory Accuracy)

Title: CBT-BENCH: Evaluating Large Language Models on Assisting Cognitive Behavior Therapy
Venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference of the Nations of the Americas Chapter of the Association for Computational Linguistics: Human Language Technologies (Volume 1: Long Papers)
Raw Eval Metrics: Accuracy, weighted Precision, weighted Recall, weighted F1, pairwise comparison with 5-point scale (A is much better than B / A is slightly better than B / A and B are about the same / B is slightly better than A / B is much better than A) mapped to -2 to 2 scale

Title: Roleplay-doh: Enabling Domain-Experts to Create LLM-simulated Patients via Eliciting and Adhering to Principles
Venue: EMNLP 2024
Temporal_Modeling_Details: No dynamic state modeling is used; principles are static rules that govern behavior across all conversation turns, without tracking changing internal states of the simulated patient.
Raw Eval Metrics: Authenticity, Stayed in Role (Role Consistency), Resembled Past Case / Resembled Typical Case, Mirrored Challenging Aspects / Challenged the Counselor, Ready as Training Partner, Recommend to Novices, M1 (Consistency with patient description and conversation history), M2 (Awkward style of speech), M3 (Principle Adherence), Overall ranking, Effectively Guide, Ease, Efficiency, Mental Demand

Title: Towards AI-Assisted Psychotherapy: Emotion-Guided Generative Interventions

Title: EmoAgent: Assessing and Safeguarding Human-AI Interaction for Mental Health Safety
Venue: Proceedings of the 2025 Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing
Temporal_Modeling_Details: The paper conducts pre- and post-interaction psychological assessments (PHQ-9, PDI, PANSS) to measure state changes, but does not model dynamic state transitions during the conversation. Assessments are performed at initialization and after the full interaction, not continuously or at multiple time points within the conversation.
Raw Eval Metrics: Deterioration Rate (R = 1/N * sum(1(Sfinal_i > Sinitial_i))); Distribution of Psychological Test Scores (histograms); Rate of Clinically Important Difference for Individual Change (PHQ-9 score increase ≥5); PHQ-9, PDI-21, and PANSS scores; Score change distributions (Δ ≤ 0, 1 ≤ Δ ≤ 2, 3 ≤ Δ ≤ 4, Δ ≥ 5)
Clinical_Theory: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT); Cognitive Conceptualization Diagram (CCD) (Beck, 2020)

Title: LLM-empowered Chatbots for Psychiatrist and Patient Simulation: Application and Evaluation
Venue: arXiv preprint (arXiv:2305.13614v1)
Raw Eval Metrics: Human evaluation (Doctor): Fluency, Empathy, Expertise, Engagement. Automatic (Doctor): diagnose acc, symptom recall, in-depth ratio, avg question num, symptom precision, avg turns, avg doc utt len, avg pat utt len, avg # of ques. Human evaluation (Patient): Realistic, Mental State, Life Experience, Expression style, Rationality. Automatic (Patient): wrong symp ratio, Distinct-1, human-like word num, robot-like word num, unmentioned symp ratio, avg turns, avg patient utt len, avg doctor utt len
Clinical_Theory: DSM-5 (Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders), Beck Depression Inventory (BDI-II)

Title: Psychological Counseling Cannot Be Achieved Overnight: Automated Psychological Counseling Through Multi-Session Conversations
Venue: arXiv preprint
Temporal_Modeling_Details: The paper models session-by-session changes through Dynamic States that capture the client's evolving recent life events, emotional state, and cognitive state across multiple sessions. An external memory module stores structured representations per client (Client Profiles, Counseling Notes capturing key session-level information including counselor observations, session goals, and counseling assignments, and Counseling Summary). At the end of each counseling session, the conversation is summarized into this memory structure to update and retain crucial information for subsequent sessions.
Raw Eval Metrics: Helpfulness, Empathy, Guidance, Coherence (basic metrics, rated 1-5); Working Alliance Inventory (WAI): Goal Agreement, Task Agreement, Emotional Bond (12 items, rated 1-5); Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS): Positive Emotion, Negative Emotion; BLEU-1, BLEU-2, F1

Title: Development and Evaluation of ClientBot: Patient-Like Conversational Agent to Train Basic Counseling Skills
Venue: Journal of Medical Internet Research
Raw Eval Metrics: Percentage of reflections; Percentage of open questions; Percentage of listening skills overall; Satisfaction scores (1-5 scale); Wilcoxon rank test

Title: PersonaGym: Evaluating Persona Agents and LLMs
Venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
Raw Eval Metrics: PersonaScore (average of task-specific scores on 1-5 scale), Action Justification score, Expected Action score, Linguistic Habits score, Persona Consistency score, Toxicity Control score, Spearman correlation (ρ), Kendall-Tau correlation (τ), Fleiss' Kappa

Title: MIND: Towards Immersive Psychological Healing with Multi-Agent Inner Dialogue
Venue: Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025
Temporal_Modeling_Details: The devil agent's cognitive distortions dynamically weaken over multiple interaction rounds based on the player's comforting words. The strategist agent evaluates whether the devil's mindset has evolved each iteration.
Raw Eval Metrics: SP Role-Playing Evaluation: Dialogue Stability, Coherence & Fluency, Emotional Expression, Personalization & Diversity, Accuracy (1-5 scale). Main Experiment: Immersion (IM), Coherence (CO), Engagement (EN), Emotional Relief (ER), Satisfaction (SA), Interest (IN) (1-5 scale). Human Experiment: Positive and Negative Affect Schedule (PANAS) - 10 positive affect dimensions and 10 negative affect dimensions.
Clinical_Theory: Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (Beck, 1979); Dialectical Behavior Therapy (Lynch et al., 2007); Emotion Regulation (Gross, 1998)

Title: Future of ADHD Care: Evaluating the Efficacy of ChatGPT in Therapy Enhancement
Venue: Healthcare
Temporal_Modeling_Details: No dynamic state modeling was implemented in the evaluation. The paper discusses Reflexion as a future approach: 'Reflexion leverages linguistic feedback in the model. This method involves language agents reflecting on their performance, storing these reflections in memory, and using this accumulated knowledge to improve decision making in subsequent attempts.' However, this was not implemented in the current evaluation.
Raw Eval Metrics: Emotional Understanding and Empathy (Insight into Patient's Emotional State, Empathetic Response to Emotional Indicators, Consistency and Appropriateness of Empathy, Validation of Patient's Experiences and Emotions, Facilitation of Safe Emotional Expression); Communication and Language (Clarity and Comprehensibility of Communication, Coherence and Relevance in Conversation, Clarity and Conciseness of Information Provided, Handling Misunderstandings, Multilingual Interaction Handling); Engagement and Motivation (Engaging and Motivational Language Usage, Engagement Level in Therapy Sessions, Promotion of Active Participation, Sustaining Patient Interest, Encouragement of Autonomy and Self-expression, Positive Session Atmosphere); Adaptability and Flexibility (Adaptability to Changing Conversation Dynamics, Response to Novel or Unexpected Inputs, Ability to Redirect Conversation, Flexibility in Conversational Style, Adjustment Based on Feedback, Incorporation of Continuous Improvement Feedback); Therapeutic Effectiveness and Suitability (Overall Effectiveness as a Therapeutic Tool, Meaningful Contributions to Therapy, Suitability for Diverse Patient Groups, Recommendation for Clinical Use, Potential for Future Applications, Compatibility with Various Therapeutic Modalities); Cultural and Sensory Sensitivity (Cultural and Linguistic Sensitivity, Responsiveness to Nonverbal Cues); Stress and Coping Support (Reduction of Patient Stress Levels, Support in Developing Coping Strategies, Enhancement of Communication Skills, Tailored and Personalized Responses); Confidentiality and Privacy (Maintaining Confidentiality and Privacy); Rapport and Trust Building (Building Trust with Patient, Rapport Establishment, Creation of a Safe Environment, Respect for Patient's Boundaries, Consistent Therapeutic Presence)
